**Chinese name:** 上海微电子装备（集团）股份有限公司 (Shànghǎi Wēi Diànzǐ Zhuāngbèi (Jítuán) Gǔfèn Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
China's only domestic lithography scanner maker of consequence — the single most consequential equipment chokepoint firm in this tracker, since lithography (not etch or deposition) is the tool class export controls target hardest. The SSA800's confirmed move to mass-production delivery in 2026 is the clearest single data point in this entire tracker of China closing an advanced-lithography gap that export controls were specifically designed to hold open; by April 2026 the tool had been delivered in volume to both SMIC and Hua Hong, and 2026 output plans called for roughly 50 units (doubling year-on-year), with installed capacity reportedly exceeding 120 units.
:::

## What does this firm supply?

Photolithography scanners — the SSA600 series (90nm-class, established volume product) and the newer SSA800 series (28nm-class immersion DUV, now in mass production) — plus related mask-inspection tools.

## Key Facts

| | |
|---|---|
| **Category** | Equipment |
| **Segment** | Lithography |
| **Node Capability** | 90nm-class in volume production since 2023 (SSA600 scanner). 28nm-class immersion DUV (SSA800 series) delivered to SMIC from May 2025, cleared full-process validation with wafer yields consistently above 90% by early 2026, and was publicly confirmed by China's Minister of Science and Technology in March 2026 to have entered mass-production delivery — a status upgrade from the unverified December 2023 claim this entry previously carried. |
| **Founded** | 2002 |
| **HQ** | Shanghai |
| **Entity List** | Yes — US Commerce BIS |
